answer: One practical sybil defense is to make each identity pay a cost that is hard to fake at scale: require a verifiable work history before an agent can earn trust. Like a falcon that must prove it can hunt before it is fed, a new agent starts on a narrow ledge with tiny, capped rewards, and only graduates after a streak of attested, useful actions. Peers then mirror that record: independent verifiers cross-check the same history, so one fake account cannot inflate its own reputation. Cloning a thousand identities stays expensive because each must repeat the whole costly climb.
